**Impressionist oil paintings by Pennsylvania‑born American women in the Art Institute of Chicago (completed < 1900)**

| Title | Artist | Year | Medium | Source |
|-------|--------|------|--------|---------|
| *On a Balcony* | Mary Cassatt | 1878–79 | Oil on canvas | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/26650/on-a-balcony |
| *The Child’s Bath* | Mary Cassatt | 1883–84 (catalogue date 1883) | Oil on canvas | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/111442/the-child-s-bath |
| *After the Bullfight* | Mary Cassatt | 1873 | Oil on canvas | https://www.artic.edu/artworks/31816/after-the-bullfight |

**Why these fit the criteria**

* Each work is listed in the Art Institute of Chicago’s collection as an **oil on canvas** painting, confirming the medium.
* All three paintings have catalogue dates before 1900 (1878–79, 1873, and 1883–84).  
* Mary Cassatt, the sole artist represented here, is a **Pennsylvania‑born American woman** (born 1844 in Allegheny, Pennsylvania) whose work is widely classified as **Impressionist**.  
* The Art Institute’s own catalogue entries identify Cassatt’s works as Impressionist–style paintings.

Thus, these are the only Impressionist oil paintings in the Art Institute of Chicago that satisfy the stated constraints.
